correctness.rationale: The combinatorial path Laplacian has simple real cosine eigenvectors phi_0=n^-1/2 and phi_k(j)=sqrt(2/n)cos(pi*k*(j+1/2)/n). For every u<v, factoring phi_k(u) +/- phi_k(v) gives a product of cosine or sine functions at indices A=u+v+1 and B=v-u, exactly one odd. Converting each factor zero to c*k = n or 0 (mod 2n), counting zero indices k=0,...,n-1 by gcd, and distinguishing even n=2^t q (odd q) from odd n (least prime p), proves sharp support (n-q+1)/2 or (n-n/p)/2 and the reflected-pair/sign/optimizer enumeration. For n a power of two, q=1 ties both signs; for n=2 and n=3 boundaries give integer counts. Inspected actual RESULT.md, check_exact.py and check_dct.py at frozen Git blobs; verified algebraic examples P6/P9/P16 and checked bound/equality logic. Script enumerates n=2..80 exactly and DCT 2..22 with high precision, but the universal conclusion rests on modular proof, not finite logs.
